evidence: Paper Section 3.2 defines DAEF formally as the abstraction phi(T) = (V_F, E_F, lambda_F) of a domain-grounded workflow, with controlled vocabulary and two-stage annotation protocol; this construct does not exist prior to SkillFlow.

Paper Section 3.4 specifies the Agentic Lifelong Learning protocol with formal equations for skill-patch generation and library update; this protocol is named and operationalized for the first time in SkillFlow.

Paper Section 3.4 'Skill patch schema' paragraph defines the three-field skill-patch record (summary, upsert_files, delete_paths) and the Apply operator as the minimal auditable interface for skill evolution; the construct is introduced by this paper.
Paper explicitly proposes and names 'bottom-up agent paradigm' as its contribution, contrasting it with top-down agent design.

Paper defines 'trial-and-reasoning' as the core skill-acquisition mechanism of the bottom-up paradigm: explore action sequences, reflect on outcomes via LLM, retain those that produce recognizable visual change.
Paper operationalizes implicit visual reward as R_semantics = M(p_differ, sigma, x_t, x_{t+1}), where an LLM judges visual diff between pre/post-execution screenshots as the sole reward signal.
Paper builds on and operationalizes the existing agentic-skill format (cites agentskills2026 as the standardized notion) and uses it as the unit of analysis throughout the evaluation.
Paper formalizes skill retrieval as a distinct evaluation stage with its own Recall@k metrics and compares direct vs. agentic retrieval strategies (Section 3.2, Table 1).

Paper introduces skill refinement (Section 4) with two formal strategies (query-agnostic, query-specific) and provides the first empirical characterization of refinement as a multiplier on existing skill quality.

The paper's central object of study is the agent skill format: 'Each skill is a structured document that encodes task-specific instructions, workflows, and domain knowledge'. The benchmark evaluates methods that generate these skills.

The paper formalizes and benchmarks the generate-store-reuse cycle as continual learning via skill generation, evaluating four method classes and documenting failure modes (recursive drift in self-feedback, adoption gap) that materially refine the concept.

Section 4.1 'Skill dependency verification' explicitly defines and formalizes skill-dependent tasks via the pass-rate inequality with R=10, alpha=0.5, plus the skill-solvability requirement. This is a new methodological concept introduced by this paper.
Section 3.1 (and Algorithm 1) explicitly proposes and names the GUI-DFS exploration algorithm as a primary contribution of the paper.
The paper introduces the 'environment-learned computer-use agent' paradigm in the introduction and frames it as a core conceptual contribution.
Section 3.2 names and defines the 'skill boundary check' mechanism as a contribution; ablations in Table 3 attribute the majority of efficiency gains to it.
Paper explicitly reframes memory operations as 'learnable and evolvable memory skills'; memory skill defined in sec Skill Bank with description + content fields.
Section 2.3 introduces span-level skill-conditioned memory construction: executor conditions on (x_t, M_t, A_t) and emits memory updates in one pass.
Section 2.5 describes the closed-loop optimization that alternates controller training and designer-driven skill-bank evolution with snapshot-and-rollback.

JARVIS-1 proposes multimodal memory as a key-value store with multimodal keys (task + visual observation) and successful plans as values, retrieved via two-stage CLIP-text then CLIP-vision similarity for situation-grounded in-context planning.

JARVIS-1 introduces a named interactive-planning scheme that interleaves self-check (upfront sub-goal precondition simulation) with self-explain (post-failure environment-feedback diagnosis), converging in 2-3 re-plan rounds vs DEPS's 6+.

JARVIS-1 uses LLM-driven self-instruct to assess current capability, propose tasks from a Minecraft task pool, execute them in parallel via speculative execution, and commit successful trajectories to a shared centralized memory for lifelong improvement without gradient updates.

AWM proposes 'agent workflow memory' which centers on an LM-based induction module I(E)->W that extracts reusable workflows from agent trajectories; section 3.3 explicitly defines workflow induction as a contribution.
AWM defines workflows as (description, step_sequence) abstract sub-routines with placeholders for example-specific entities; section 3.2 'Workflow Representation' specifies the artifact AWM produces.

The paper proposes and names CER as its central contribution: 'we propose Contextual Experience Replay (CER), a training-free framework to enable efficient self-improvement for language agents in their context window.'
AtomMem explicitly proposes atomic CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) as the minimal action space for memory management, citing completeness, atomic minimality, and task-agnosticness.
Paper reframes memory management as a learnable decision-making problem in a POMDP formulation and optimizes the memory policy end-to-end via GRPO.
Paper proposes a hybrid retrieval mechanism combining a deterministic scratchpad entry returned every step with selective TopK query-based retrieval from a vector store.

MemWeaver introduces the tri-layer memory consolidation framework (Graph Memory + Experience Memory + Passage Memory) with explicit cross-layer structural edges as the central architectural contribution.
Paper introduces Live-Evo as 'the first online self-evolving memory system that learns from a stream of incoming data over time' and contrasts it explicitly with traditional offline self-evolution.
Paper proposes the Meta-Guideline Bank as a higher-level memory layer holding composition meta-heuristics, decoupling 'what happened' from 'how to use it'.
Paper introduces 'Verify Before Update': candidate experiences are only committed to the bank when a re-evaluation shows a statistically significant improvement over the original memory-on score.

Paper explicitly proposes 'collective skill evolution' as the central framing and names it as a distinguishing property: 'SkillClaw enables collective evolution, where knowledge from individual interactions contributes to a shared and continuously improving skill ecosystem.'

Paper introduces 'an agentic evolver' as the open-ended LLM-driven update operator: 'SkillClaw instantiate an agentic evolver, an LLM agent equipped with a structured harness ... The harness provides structured inputs but does not constrain the evolver's reasoning.' Listed as one of three distinguishing properties (agentic evolution paradigm).

The paper explicitly proposes Subagent Pattern as one of two new pattern forms: 'we introduce Subagent Pattern extraction... encapsulates them as specialized subagents... maintain their own memory and state management'.
Memp proposes the Build/Retrieve/Update factorization as the design space for procedural memory and frames each module as an independently varied optimization knob.
Section 'Procedural memory exhibits transferability from strong models to weaker ones' empirically demonstrates GPT-4o's memory bank improving Qwen2.5-14B on TravelPlanner and ALFWorld.
Memp Section 'Memory Update' formalizes U(M(t),E(t),tau_t) and contrasts Vanilla, Validation, and Adjustment update operators.
Paper Section 3.1 formalizes the Skill-augmented MDP (Skill-MDP) as a 6-tuple extending classical MDP with a dynamic Skill pool, explicitly listed as the first of three core contributions.

Paper Section 4.1 introduces Semantic Gradients as natural-language update directions for Skill components extracted via hindsight attribution; positioned as a novel contrast to TextGrad which targets static variables for instantaneous response quality.
Paper Section 3 defines a Skill as the reusable procedural unit triple <activation, execution, termination> and lists Procedural Skill Formalization as its first contribution.
Paper introduces JitRL as a training-free framework for test-time policy optimization without gradient updates; positions the technique as a new RL formulation operating purely at inference time.

Paper defines M = {(s_i, a_i, G_i)} as a dynamic non-parametric memory used in place of a trained value network for test-time value estimation; this is a central conceptual contribution beyond the specific JitRL pipeline.

Theorem 4.1 derives the additive logit update z'(s,a) = z(s,a) + β·A(s,a) as the exact closed-form solution of the KL-constrained policy optimization objective; the paper presents this as the core theoretical contribution.
Voyager: an automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration by prompting GPT-4 to propose next task from agent state
ever-growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving complex behaviors indexed by description embedding
novel iterative prompting mechanism incorporating environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification for program improvement
we instantiate another GPT-4 agent for self-verification; act as a critic and inform whether the program achieves the task
MemEvolve frames the memory architecture itself as the search object via bilevel meta-evolution over a candidate set.
Decomposes any memory system as Omega=(Encode, Store, Retrieve, Manage); 12 baselines re-implemented under one BaseMemoryProvider interface.
Bilevel loop: inner = experience accumulation under fixed arch; outer = Pareto select + diagnose-and-design over architectures.
Generalizes Memp's Build/Retrieve/Update three-axis cartography to a four-slot E/U/R/G genotype usable for meta-evolutionary search.
